spec:
eShram CONSTELLATION: FINAL BUILD SPEC (design lead, 2026-09-04)

0. PREMISE AND HONESTY LINE
341,854,283 registrations cannot be drawn. The device: 1 mote = 10,000 registrations (K=10,000), printed in the legend and the mast. Sizes and motes use STATE-CALIBRATED counts (district total x calibration_factors.factor[state]; sum 317,403,974, the eShram dashboard's distinct-UAN total). The 24,450,309 dump rows above that total are the BELT (2,445 dots). 31,740 pack motes + 2,445 belt dots = 34,185 = 341.85M / K: every dump row is a mote-share exactly once, nothing drawn twice. Every label says 'registrations', never 'workers' (self-enrolment with scheme incentives). Mast: 'eShram Constellation · 341,854,283 registrations · 36 states, N districts · every mote is 10,000 people'. Sub: 'scaled to the dashboard's 317.4M distinct UANs (state factors 0.72 Karnataka .. 1.03 Puducherry); the belt is the 24.5M-row difference'.

1. NODES (engine: buckets = hubs, clusters = satellites)
HUBS = 36 states/UTs from district_summary.state. Hub is an UNSIZED ANCHOR: r = 5 world units fixed, ink ring as today, small filled disc carries the state-level scalar in Women/Literacy modes. Size channel lives on districts only (they sum to the state anyway). This resolves the 'half of UP sits under its own hub disc' refutation and the double-count of hub area + district area.
SATELLITES = district_summary rows AFTER cleanup: (a) DROP the 12 rows with total < 100 (AP: ADILABAD 1, HYDERABAD 1, KHAMMAM 3, NALGONDA 10, WARANGAL 3 = Telangana twins under the old AP code; J&K KARGIL 1; SIKKIM SOUTH 1; MH RAIGARH 13; builder lists the rest); their ~40 registrations are added to the belt remainder so the 341,854,283 identity holds. (b) MERGE spelling twins within a state via an explicit MERGE dict applied to EVERY table before aggregation: CHHATTISGARH KABEERDHAM->KABIRDHAM, DAKSHIN BASTAR DANTEWADA->DANTEWADA, BALODABAZAR-BHATAPARA->BALODA BAZAR, GAURELA-PENDRA-MARWAHI->GAURELLA PENDRA MARWAHI; SIKKIM SOUTH->SOUTH DISTRICT; WEST BENGAL NORTH 24 PARGANAS->24 PARAGANAS NORTH, MALDA->MALDAH, PASCHIM MEDINIPUR->MEDINIPUR WEST, COOCH BEHAR->COOCHBEHAR; MAHARASHTRA AHILYANAGAR->AHMEDNAGAR. Expected satellite count 822 +-3; the builder prints the exact N into the mast and the title. Never hardcode 844.
SIZE (districts): r = 0.0065 * sqrt(n_cal) world units, floor 1.2 (floor bites under 34,000 registrations; builder prints how many). Median district (277k raw, ~263k cal) 3.3; largest (Murshidabad, 2.38M cal) 10.0. At the geo fit scale (~0.7) the median disc is ~2.3 px: the fit view is the 'regions' view; districts arrive on zoom. Discs under 5 px are FLAT-FILLED (no body gradient, no glow) in both engines: skill rule and a 2x draw saving. Legend size key printed 'at 1x zoom': 100k = 2.1, 1M = 6.5, 2.4M = 10 (world px).
Ring channel: ring = state anchor only. Districts never ringed. Hollow disc = no data for the active field (0 registrations in the scrubbed group; unclassified in Work mode).

2. COLOUR MODES (4 buttons: Women · Work · Literacy · Corridors; Structure dropped, Corridors is structure + lit edges). Recolour never moves anything; 200 ms paint tween as today.
2a. WOMEN (default). Diverging on female share of registrations with ONE zero for discs and motes: PARITY 50%. t = clamp((fem - 0.50)/0.17, -1, +1); domain 33% orange #cf6e40 .. 50% mid #787885 .. 67% teal #2f9e8b (the engine's validated void pair). District p5-p95 = 43.7-67.1, so ~5% saturate teal (say so). India's 54.8% is a printed TICK on the legend bar, not the pivot. Why parity: the refutations showed a 54.8 pivot paints 240 districts holding 142M registrations (42%) orange while their own packs are teal-majority; with parity, teal on a disc and teal in its dust mean the same thing (more women than men). Cost accepted: Haryana 48.6 / Gujarat 48.4 read near-neutral, which is true. Hub disc = state female share (sum female / sum total, raw rows). Mote = its OWN gender: value10 +10 = 10,000 women -> teal pole, -10 = men -> orange pole (dustColors n10 -> t = n10/10). Legend: '33% <- 50% parity -> 67% · India 54.8% (tick) · teal disc = more women than men among registrants · teal dot = 10,000 women, orange dot = 10,000 men · share of REGISTRATIONS, not of the workforce · clamped, ~5% of districts saturate'. Small-n rule (replaces 5/20): n < 1,000 -> MID; 1,000..10,000 -> lerp(MID, colour, (n-1000)/9000); >= 10,000 full; n = 0 hollow. Stored: node.health = t, node.fem = raw share, node.n = calibrated, node.n_raw.
2b. WORK (categorical). District disc = rq6_district_types.dest_type (LQ k-means: Agricultural 322, Construction 170, Domestic/Care 121, Services/Urban 101, Manufacturing 83, Artisanal 7; 40 unclassified -> hollow, tooltip 'not classified: below typology floor'). NEVER 'top occupation' (agriculture is modal in 780 of 844). Hubs = STRUCT ink (states have no class; legend says so). Motes = their OWN occupation group g (0..6, the 35->7 table below). One hue table serves classes and groups so disc and dust vocabularies agree: 0 Agriculture/Agricultural #a9ab54 · 1 Construction & mining/Construction #dc9064 · 2 Domestic & care/Domestic-Care #a498e5 · 3 Manufacturing #50b1dc · 4 Artisanal #d887ae · 5 Services & urban/Services-Urban #51bb9a · 6 Miscellaneous #787885 (grey on purpose; motes only). Legend: 'disc = what the district does MORE than India does (LQ class) · dots = what its people actually do · colour groups, labels identify' plus swatch rows with national share: Agriculture 51.5%, Manufacturing 14.4%, Domestic & care 10.9%, Construction & mining 9.3%, Services & urban 8.1%, Miscellaneous 5.0%, Artisanal 0.9%. Tooltip prints both: 'top: Agriculture 61% · specialises: Construction (LQ 2.1)'. Validate the 7 hues as adjacent pairs on #101014 and #05070c with dataviz validate_palette before shipping.
Group table (35 -> 7): 0 AGRICULTURE. 1 CONSTRUCTION, MINING. 2 DOMESTIC AND HOUSEHOLD WORKERS, HEALTHCARE, BEAUTY & WELLNESS. 3 APPAREL, CAPITAL GOODS & MANUFACTURING, LEATHER INDUSTRY WORKS, ELECTRONICS & HW, TOBACCO INDUSTRY, FOOD INDUSTRY, GEM & JEWELLERY, PRINTING, GLASS & CERAMICS, TOOL MAKERS AND RELATED WORKERS. 4 HANDICRAFTS & CARPETS, TEXTILE & HANDLOOM, WOOD & CARPENTRY, MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS, CARPENTERS AND JOINERS. 5 AUTOMOBILE & TRANSPORTATION, EDUCATION, TOURISM & HOSPITALITY, OFFICE ADMINISTRATION & FACILITY MANAGEMENT, RETAIL, ORGANISED RETAIL, PRIVATE SECURITY, PROFESSIONALS, SERVICE, BFSI, BANKING FINANCIAL SERVICES & INSURANCE. 6 MISCELLANEOUS, OTHERS, NOT PROVIDED. Builder asserts every primary_occupation string in district_occupation_gender is mapped and the 7 sums equal 341,854,283 (verified: 175,986,343 / 31,652,258 / 37,112,492 / 49,255,296 / 3,138,002 / 27,682,902 / 17,026,990).
2c. LITERACY (sequential). s = district_education count[education == 'NOT LITERATE'] / sum(count) per district; hub = state sums. t = clamp((s - 0.03)/0.39, 0, 1); ramp MID #787885 -> amber #f0b429 (brighter = more not-literate; a dark low end vanished into the void per refutation). Domain 3%..42% (district p5 4.7, p50 19.0, p95 41.7; national 22.73%). Legend anchors: Kerala 1.3%, Maharashtra 11.7%, UP 28.2%, Bihar 34.2%, Telangana 36.3%; line 'pivot-free ramp · Moran I 0.73: expect blocks'. Motes take the parent's colour (education is not observed per mote). One definition of illiterate everywhere: NOT LITERATE only; the panel's edu5 strip labels the other band 'literate, no schooling'. Validate the ramp on both voids.
2d. CORRIDORS (structure + flow). All discs and motes STRUCT ink #9b98b0; corridor edges at full alpha; member edges 0.10; belt 0.10. NO node colour for migrant share: the sequential in-migrant share was refuted twice (711 of ~822 discs one grey; the brightest hubs are micro-UTs, Maharashtra nearly black under its own corridors). Flow lives on edges; numbers live in the hub tooltip (in / out / net) and panel.

3. EDGES (two types, one corridor hue #a88bfa, grey membership)
3a. bucket_edges[] = DIRECTED inter-state corridors from migration_matrix.csv, permanent_state != current_state, PUDUCHERRY folded into PONDICHERRY first (1,084 corridors, 878,505 movers). Row {a: origin state id, b: destination state id, n: count, back: reverse count or 0, w, forced: bool}. Inclusion: n >= 2,000 (82 rows, 81.0% of movers) UNION each origin's single largest corridor when that is below 2,000 (18 rows, e.g. Kerala->Tamil Nadu 941, Himachal->Punjab 1,538) = 100 directed rows; every hub has degree >= 1; drawn as ~82 undirected lines (64 pairs above threshold, 18 of them reciprocal, + 18 forced). Weight w = clamp(log10(gross/2000)/log10(73928/2000), 0, 1), gross = n + back (UP<->Maharashtra 73,928 -> 1). Paint: width = (0.6 + 1.6 w) * P.linkWidth; alpha FIXED per mode (Corridors 0.55, other modes 0.22, hover set 0.8, outside hover/search set 0.05); DIRECTION = createLinearGradient along the edge from origin at 0.25 x alpha to destination at 1.0 x alpha (bright end = receiver; median asymmetry 6.2x so it is unambiguous). The 5 pairs with max/min < 2 (Delhi-Haryana 1.03, UP-MP 1.11, UP-WB 1.12, Kerala-TN 1.31, MH-Telangana 1.32) draw uniform alpha, tooltip 'two-way'. No arrowheads, no marching dashes: the view at rest must be dots-with-lines. Springs: force layout k = 0.006, rest = rEff_a + rEff_b + 90 + (1-w)*400; geo layout k = 0 (edges are paint; the -0.86 distance elasticity shows as short bright vs long faint lines).
3b. edges_in[] = origin STATE -> destination DISTRICT from district_migrant_origin.csv, permanent_state != current_state, count >= 2,000: 78 edges, 45.3% of inter-state movers, landing on 41 districts from 10 origins (verified: UP->Gurugram 21,430, Thane 18,269, Surat 16,797, Mumbai 12,839; Bihar->Gurugram 17,993, Surat 12,122, Gautam Buddha Nagar 9,948). Row {a: state id, b: district id, n, w on the same log scale}. Drawn ONLY while a hub is hovered or pinned, same gradient, width 0.6+1.0w, alpha 0.6; their targets join the hub's hover set (nbr[hub] += edges_in targets). This is the fix for the refuted 'corridors land on Gurugram' claim: without it the page's premise is false.
3c. DASHED [3,5] carries exactly ONE meaning: forced = the origin's top corridor under 2,000 movers ('thin evidence, kept so no state is an orphan'). Calibration flags and geo provenance are tooltip text, never a stroke. Member edges (district -> state): solid 0.7 px rgba(110,108,132,.22), 0.05 when Satellites filter is off; in geo mode they are drawn only in the hover set (a map does not need 822 spokes).
Legend edge key: '- - district to its state (hover) · ▬ corridor >= 2,000 movers · fades from sender, bright at receiver · width = log volume · 82 drawn = 81% of 878,505 inter-state registrations · dashed = top corridor under 2,000 · hover a state: its origin -> district corridors (>= 2,000)'.
Hub tooltip: in / out / net (Haryana +95,223, Maharashtra +93,819, Delhi +93,383, Gujarat +86,690 ... Bihar -191,662, UP -195,720; Arunachal +20,294 is a receiver, say so). Hub panel: 'Top corridors out' and 'in' (5 each, count, 'not drawn' below threshold, clickable refocus), net balance, and the gravity line as TEXT: 'distance elasticity -0.86 · common language x1.67 · movers +5.4 pp more educated'.

4. MOTES
1 mote = 10,000 registrations, state-calibrated. CELL = (district, occupation group g, gender s) from district_occupation_gender.csv. Allocation by largest remainder in two stages: stage 1 district quotas from n_cal/K summing to exactly 31,740 (74 districts under ~5,000 calibrated get 0; median 26; max 238 Murshidabad); stage 2 within a district, cells get q_d x count_cell / total, summing to exactly q_d. Transgender (9,867 rows, 0.003%) never reaches a mote; legend says so. Format unchanged: dust[districtId] = [[value10, g], ...], value10 = +10 female / -10 male, g = group index 0..6 (this is the slot the engine already treats as the scrub index and the 3D stratum). No 'b:' hub packs. Expected split: ~17,380 female / ~14,360 male; by group ~16,382 / 2,947 / 3,457 / 4,616 / 187 / 2,610 / 1,533 (+-10 after Hamilton). Colour: Women -> own gender pole; Work -> group hue by g; Literacy / Corridors -> parent district colour (the engine's per-group sprite path); scrub-lit motes x1.6 size alpha 1, others 0.11 (existing behaviour). Belt = 2,445 dots, arc in state-ordered segments proportional to each state's gap (Maharashtra 5.94M, Karnataka 4.36M lead) so a belt tooltip can read 'Maharashtra: 24.5M rows, 18.6M official'. Legend, always on: '· = 10,000 registrations (state-calibrated) · 31,740 motes' and 'belt = 2,445 dots = 24.5M dump rows above the dashboard's 317.4M distinct UANs: estimated duplicate mass by state factor, an upper bound, not an exclusion list'. Tooltip: '26 motes = 263,000 registrations (calibrated; dump 277,326 x 0.95)'. Budget: 31,740 + 2,445 = 34,185 dust points; 3D ~13 ms/frame on M2 by extrapolation from 18,066 = 6.6 ms; density slider default 1.0, auto 0.6 when navigator.hardwareConcurrency < 8 or innerWidth < 900.

5. SCRUB AXIS = OCCUPATION GROUP (no time exists). Chosen over age band because district x occupation x gender is OBSERVED (district_occupation_gender), the 7 stops are all meaningful (age had a dead 60+ stop with 3,772 rows and a 1.4% <18 stop), and it carries the headline read. DATA.axis = ['Agriculture','Construction & mining','Domestic & care','Manufacturing','Artisanal','Services & urban','Miscellaneous'] (fixed order = 3D strata floor to ceiling); the JSON key stays `months` so the dock needs no rewiring; mLab becomes identity. series[state][label] = [t, n, fem] and cluster_series[district][label] = [t, n, fem] with t on the same parity transform, n = raw registrations in that group. composite[g] = [label, t_national, n, fem]: Agriculture 0.505, Construction & mining 0.271, Domestic & care 0.923, Manufacturing 0.641, Artisanal 0.528, Services & urban 0.371, Miscellaneous 0.711. Default position = Σ all. Scrub live in Women mode only (dockGuard switches to Women). At a stop: disc = female share within that group in that node (small-n rule; hollow when 0 registrations in the group); motes of group g lit, others 0.11; 3D lights the stratum. Dock: big label 'Domestic & care · 10.9% of registrations · 92.3% women'; sparkline replaced by 7 LINEAR bars (share of registry, 1 px floor, percentage printed; sqrt height was refuted) filled with the group's national female share on the diverging scale, current stop outlined; Play steps 900 ms per stop 0..6 then Σ. FLAGS: Artisanal '0.9% of the registry: ~365 districts under 1,000 shown grey'; Miscellaneous 'residual: Miscellaneous, Others, Not provided'; Domestic & care 'saturates teal by design: national 92.3%; within-trade spread is in the panel'. Zero fixed at parity at every stop (no moving pivot: one rule, one legend); the within-trade spread (Construction p5-p95 9-47%) lives in the pinned panel's 7-bar strip with national reference ticks. Age band (7) and education (5) are NOT scrubbed: they render as bar strips in the detail panel (clusters[].age7, edu5; buckets[].age7, edu5), the 60+ bar drawn empty with 'eShram enrols ages 16-59'.

6. LAYOUT: GEO-ANCHORED DEFAULT, POSITION BLEND (not force blend)
Geometry source: the mapgen 2024 all-India shapefile (Survey of India / LGD, DISTRICT_BOUNDARY.shp 820 districts + STATE_BOUNDARY.shp), NOT GADM (594 polygons, pre-2014, 60% match, six states at zero). Measured today: after fixing five garbled STATE_UT strings (Karn<taka, UTTAR>KHAND, CHHATISGARH, Lakshadweep-UT, A&N) and mapping encoding damage ('>'->A, '|'->I) plus mapgen aliases.py and token-sort fuzzy >= 80, 787 of 844 rows match (93.5% of registrations). A ~35-entry hand alias table (West Bengal reversed word order: MURSHIDABAD, 24 PARAGANAS NORTH, MEDINIPUR EAST/WEST, MALDAH, COOCHBEHAR, HOWRAH; Karnataka new names RAICHUR, DHARWAD, TUMAKURU, YADGIR; MP old names EAST NIMAR, HOSHANGABAD; AP SPSR NELLORE, Y.S.R.; TN TUTICORIN; Odisha BALESHWAR, SONEPUR) must close this to >= 810 of ~822 (>= 98% of registrations) before ship. Match table with tiers at scratchpad/match_table.json. Unmatched districts sit at the state centroid + golden-angle offset (radius 8 + 3 sqrt(i)) with matched:false and tooltip 'position: state centroid, no boundary match' (text, not a dash).
Projection: equirectangular, 36 world units per degree: x = (lon - 82.5) * 36, y = -(lat - 22.5) * 36 (India ~1,044 x 1,044 world units). 36/deg keeps the largest packs inside their land: UP needs ~22,500 sq units for 8,453 motes against ~28,400 of land (0.79 fill), Bihar 0.78, West Bengal 0.68; Delhi overflows (5x) and is capped per district (below). District target = representative_point of its polygon; state target = representative_point of STATE_BOUNDARY (table: UP 80.78,27.14 · Bihar 86.12,25.90 · Maharashtra 75.43,18.82 · WB 88.06,24.39 · MP 79.39,23.97 · Rajasthan 73.83,26.63 · Karnataka 75.53,15.03 · Gujarat 71.99,22.42 · Odisha 84.48,20.19 · AP 79.62,15.90 · TN 78.35,10.82 · Jharkhand 85.17,23.66 · Chhattisgarh 81.51,20.94 · Assam 90.76,26.05 · Kerala 76.43,10.54 · Punjab 75.58,31.03 · Haryana 76.05,29.29 · Telangana 79.30,17.88 · Delhi 77.12,28.64 · J&K 74.93,33.70 · Uttarakhand 79.32,30.09 · HP 77.35,31.82 · Tripura 91.65,23.74 · Manipur 93.87,24.76 · Meghalaya 91.26,25.57 · Arunachal 95.00,28.06 · Nagaland 94.56,26.12 · Goa 74.10,15.35 · Mizoram 92.87,23.23 · Chandigarh 76.78,30.73 · Sikkim 88.46,27.60 · Pondicherry 79.81,10.92 · DNH&DD 70.93,20.72 · Ladakh 77.66,34.72 · A&N 92.49,10.71 · Lakshadweep 73.68,10.81). State anchors never depend on district matching.
Mechanics: every node keeps two coordinate sets: (gx, gy) fixed targets and (fx, fy) force-simulated. Drawn position = P.geo * (gx,gy) + (1 - P.geo) * (fx,fy). Forces slider 'Map <-> Force' = P.geo, 0..1, default 1.0, live readout. The physics NEVER sees the geo targets, so sibling repulsion cannot blow the outline apart (the refuted 1,000x arithmetic). At P.geo = 1 the tick is skipped entirely (0 ms physics); at P.geo < 1 the force sim runs as today with hierarchical repulsion. Moving the slider morphs positions smoothly (honey); mental map survives. In geo mode node-drag is disabled (drag = pan); in force mode drag as today. Recolour, filter, scrub never move anything. Legend line whenever P.geo > 0: 'positions: 2024 boundary centroids (LGD), blended toward physics by the slider; not a map'. Zoom clamp 0.35..8 in geo (labels need it), 0.35..4 in force.
Dust in geo: phyllotaxis around the district centroid with a per-district radius cap = 0.6 x distance to the nearest other district centroid (k = min(0.92, cap / sqrt(N))), so Delhi and Gurugram pack denser instead of spilling; the sprite blit uses 'source-over' in geo (the 'lighter' blit would turn the Gangetic plain into a white slab) and 'lighter' in force mode.
Hub footprint for physics (force mode only): hierarchical repulsion: hub-hub all pairs (630) with hub rEff = member rest + max child dustR (the visible shell, per the skill); satellite-satellite among siblings only (~15k pairs); satellite-foreign hub (~30k) => ~45k pair checks instead of 387k. Both engines.
3D (3d.src.html): geo mode places nodes on the ground plane (engine x = gx, z = gy, y = 0), no physics, camera pitch -0.6, spin default 0 (auto-rotating a map disorients; slider stays), fitted distance. HEIGHT = TRADE STRATUM for motes and nothing else: mote y-offset = -(g - 3) * 22 + jitter(+-7) world units, xy = phyllotaxis disc around its district, so India is a seven-layer slab: Agriculture the thick floor (51%), Services & urban and Miscellaneous the thin ceiling; the scrub lights one floor. Force mode keeps the fibonacci-shell layout but motes still stratify by g, so the z meaning never changes. HUD line: 'height = trade stratum: agriculture floor, services ceiling; nodes on the ground'. Net migration balance is NOT a height (dropped: it hit the clamp on UP and Bihar and double-loaded the axis); it stays in the tooltip.

7. LABELS (822 satellites)
Hubs: 36 labels persistent, placed first in registrations-desc order through the existing 8 slots; a hub label that fails every slot is DROPPED unless the hub is top-12 by n (remove the slots[0] fallback for kind 'bucket'); it returns on zoom. Legend: 'zoom in for small-state labels' (the 7 NE hubs and Chandigarh/Goa/DNH will drop at fit). Districts: viewport-culled and tested only when r * scale > 2.5 px; alpha = clamp((scale - P.textFade)/0.35), textFade default 1.6 (slider 1.0..3.0); between 1.6 and 2.6 only districts with n >= 300,000 get labels, above 2.6 all; hover / pinned / search hits always. Slot order below, above, right, left, far pair; no free slot = no label. Search hay = district name + state + typology class + top-3 occupations (so 'domestic' finds Domestic/Care districts).

8. TOOLTIP AND PANEL
Tooltip: name; 'district in Uttar Pradesh · 1.42M registrations (calibrated 1.39M) · 139 motes' or 'state · 84.5M registrations (dashboard) · 75 districts'; the active-mode value coloured by its own encoding (Women: '57.1% women' ; Work: 'top Agriculture 61% · specialises Construction LQ 2.1'; Literacy: 'not literate 28.2%'; Corridors hub: 'in 12,340 · out 207,900 · net -195,720'); one caveat (n < 10,000 'small district'; n < 1,000 'tone unstable'; typ -1 'not classified'; matched:false 'sits at state centroid'; state factor < 0.80 'dump 24-28% above official'). Pinned panel, district: 7-bar female-share-by-trade strip with national ticks, top-5 occupations with share and female share, top-3 origin states, LQ class, age7 and edu5 strips, '-> state' button. Hub: state factor line, in/out/net, top corridors out and in (5 each, clickable), modal-class text, age7/edu5 strips.

9. THREE HEADLINE READS (the page must make these obvious without a click, one click, and three clicks)
R1 (default: Women, geo): the teal south and east against a near-parity north-west. Tamil Nadu 65.6%, Karnataka 61.0, Kerala 60.9, Bihar 58.7, Maharashtra 58.7 teal; Haryana 48.6, Gujarat 48.4, MP 49.8 faint orange; Lakshadweep 39.9 the one deep orange; Moran I +0.55 visible as blocks that mostly stop at state borders (a registration regime, not a labour-market fact: the legend's 'registrations, not workforce' clause carries this). And the non-finding worth showing: female share does NOT sort senders from receivers (Bihar and Maharashtra both 58.7).
R2 (three clicks on the dock): TRADE sets the level, place sets the spread. Scrub to Domestic & care and the whole country flips teal (92.3% women); Construction & mining flips it orange (27.1%); the aggregate map only spans 44-67% (p5-p95). Invisible in a table, obvious in three clicks; the panel bars then show the within-trade spread (Construction: TN 47.6% vs UP 22.7%).
R3 (Corridors mode, hover UP or Bihar): one Hindi-belt funnel. UP + Bihar are 57% of 878,505 inter-state movers; Haryana, Maharashtra, Delhi, Gujarat, Punjab absorb 79% of net inflow; the hover lights origin -> district corridors onto Gurugram (UP 21,430, Bihar 17,993), Thane, Surat, Mumbai, Gautam Buddha Nagar; ten rim states hang off a single dashed corridor. Switch to Women with the pin held: the endpoints are mixed (Gurugram 44.6% orange, Surat 46.9, Mumbai 44.7; Thane 57.2 teal, Bengaluru Urban 61.0): corridors carry no gender signature. Bonus read in Literacy: Kerala 1.3% against Bihar 34.2 / Telangana 36.3, Moran I 0.73 as blocks.

10. ORDERED IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCE
1. geo/aliases: extract the mapgen shapefile, fix the 5 state strings and the '>'/'|' encoding, write eshram_geo_aliases.py (state SA map, MERGE dict, DROP list, ~35 district aliases); target >= 810/822 matched, >= 98% of registrations; emit match_report.csv with tier per row.
2. builder eshram_payload.py (pandas): load 9 CSVs; apply MERGE/DROP to every table; fold PUDUCHERRY; compute calibrated n; Hamilton motes (assert sum 31,740 and per-district exactness); belt 2,445; group map (assert all 35 occupations mapped, 7 sums = 341,854,283); series/cluster_series/composite; bucket_edges (100) + edges_in (78); geo targets; typology, LQ, literacy, age7, edu5, corridors lists for panels; write eshram_data.json and a counts.json the mast reads. Assertions fail the build, never warn.
3. 2D engine edits (index.html) in the order listed in engine_edits: schema and constants; sizing; geo blend and hierarchical tick; dust cap and compositing; edges (gradient, edges_in, forced dash); modes and resolve; scrub axis; labels; tooltip/panel/legend/mast; charts below the fold replaced (composite -> 7-group bars; small multiples -> 36 state strips of female share by trade; distress and month table deleted).
4. 3D engine edits (3d.src.html): same schema; geo ground plane + strata; hierarchical repulsion for force mode; four modes; slider max 6; density auto; HUD/legend line; tooltip copy.
5. Palette validation: run dataviz validate_palette on #101014 and #05070c for the Women poles, the 7 Work hues (adjacent pairs), the Literacy ramp; record passing hexes in the payload meta.
6. Perf pass on M2 and one Intel iGPU: geo default 2D <= 8 ms/frame, 3D <= 14 ms at density 1.0; verify the flat-fill-under-5px rule and the skipped tick at P.geo = 1.
7. Copy review with one PIF reader: the parity-pivot legend, the belt line, the 'registrations not workforce' clause, the Work two-statement line, the dashed-edge meaning.
8. Quality bar from the skill: screenshot at rest is dots-with-lines; hover set < 100 ms; zoom-out reads as regions; 2x zoom labels fade in with no overlap; recolour moves nothing; reduced-motion static but complete.

Calibrated vs raw counts: encoding and narrative lenses used calibrated; structure lens used raw motes plus a belt (double-drawing 24.45M). Winner: calibrated everywhere (encoding lens), belt = gap, 'registrations' wording (structure refutation).

Default mode pivot: encoding and structure lenses pivoted at 54.8; the narrative refutation demanded parity 50 so disc hue and mote majority agree. Winner: narrative refutation (parity zero for discs and motes; 54.8 as a tick). The encoding refutation's alternative (motes take the parent colour) lost because it discards the 'teal dot = 10,000 women' device that carries read R2.

Scrub axis: encoding and structure lenses chose age band; narrative lens chose occupation group. Winner: narrative (observed jointly with gender per district; 7 live stops; carries the trade-vs-place read; the age axis had a dead 60+ stop and a modelled joint would be needed to light motes by age). Age and education become panel strips (narrative).

Moving pivot per scrub stop (refutation notes of both encoding and narrative lenses) vs a fixed zero: fixed parity zero wins to keep one zero for disc and mote; the within-trade spread is explicitly delegated to the panel strip. Logged as an accepted loss.

Edge threshold and forced corridors: encoding lens 2,000 (82) + hover-only 500..2,000 (107); structure lens 2,000 + 18 forced (100); narrative lens 1,000 (120). Winner: structure (2,000 + 18 forced, every hub degree >= 1) because 1,000 adds 38 edges for 6 pp of movers and clutters the map; the encoding lens's hover-only thin set is dropped in favour of edges_in (origin -> district), which the encoding refutation proved necessary.

Dash meaning: encoding lens = geo provenance; structure lens = forced sub-threshold corridor; narrative lens = calibration flag. Winner: structure (one meaning, tied to the edge itself); the other two become tooltip text.

Direction: all three used the origin-faint -> destination-bright gradient; narrative added arrowheads in Corridors mode, structure added a marching dash. Winner: gradient only (obsidian-graph 'dots with lines' and reduced-motion); the structure refutation's 'width = weight, alpha fixed, gradient = direction' split is adopted.

Migrant share as node colour: encoding (sequential 0..10%), structure (sqrt 0..2%), narrative (sqrt 0..10%) all offered it; both refutations showed it blank or misleading. Winner: none; Corridors mode carries flow on edges with STRUCT nodes.

Literacy ramp: encoding lens diverging around 22.7%; structure lens #4a4a5a -> amber; narrative lens gold -> plum (bright = literate). Winner: sequential MID -> amber, bright = more not-literate (measured field brighter; the structure refutation killed the dark low end; the encoding lens's diverging pivot at 22.7 misreads because the district median is 19.0).

Work mode disc/dust disagreement (LQ class vs actual jobs in 439 districts): narrative refutation offered ring-carried typology; rejected because rings are the hub-identity channel. Winner: both statements kept, legend line 'disc = specialisation (LQ), dots = actual jobs', tooltip prints both.

Layout: encoding lens force-blended geo with district gravity; structure lens geo hubs only with free satellites; narrative lens force-blended geo for both. Narrative refutation proved force-blending cannot hold the outline; the mapgen 2024 shapefile (measured 93.5% of registrations matched) removes the GADM objection. Winner: geo default for hubs AND districts by POSITION blend (narrative refutation's fix) with physics only on the force coordinates; structure lens's 'satellites never anchored' loses because read R1 (teal bleeding across borders) needs district positions.

World scale: encoding and narrative 28 units/deg, structure 38. Winner: 36 (footprint arithmetic: UP packs fill 0.79 of its land at 36, 1.9x at 28) plus a per-district pack radius cap for Delhi-type overflow.

3D height: encoding lens = state net balance; structure lens = nothing; narrative lens = occupation stratum. Winner: narrative (coherent with the scrub; the net-balance height clamped on UP and Bihar and double-loaded the axis).

Physics for 880 nodes: all three required hierarchical repulsion; the structure refutation corrected hub rEff to the visible shell. Winner: structure refutation's rEff = member rest + max child dustR; additionally the tick is skipped entirely at P.geo = 1, which none proposed.

Legacy rows and spelling twins: encoding lens kept them as neutral floor discs; structure lens flagged 'legacy row'; both refutations said merge or drop. Winner: drop rows < 100, merge twins via an explicit dict, print the exact district count.
